summary.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 FY27: PAT up 22% QoQ to ₹375 crore, ROA 2.18%, credit cost down to 2.19%, AUM ₹74,008 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as an inflection point, with AUM up about 10.4% QoQ to ₹74,008 crore and PAT of ₹375 crore (up 21.8% QoQ). NIM plus fees rose 16 bps QoQ to 9.26%, while credit cost fell to 2.19% from 2.40-2.41% and GNPA fell to 1.20% from 1.37%. Opex-to-average AUM rose to 4.15% on frontloaded investments in collections, AI and gold branches, which management said sits within the 10-25 bps guided range. New products contributed 28% of disbursements, and the company is still building cross-sell.

segments.name: Prime Personal Loans (digital)
segments.commentary: Now 42% of PL disbursements (38% in Q1); average monthly disbursement about ₹577 crore, up 8% QoQ.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Quarterly disbursements ₹1,066 crore vs ₹875 crore in Q1; network rose to 550 branches from 460, with 90 added in the quarter and about 200 planned for FY27.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement ₹127 crore; channel partners up to 1,250 from 1,100, across 90+ locations in 13 states.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement ₹218 crore; consultant network at 700 partners; about 35% of sanctions fully digital.

segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: Quarterly disbursement ₹606 crore vs ₹433 crore in Q1; 20,000 dealers across 360 locations.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost expected to keep sloping down and gradually stabilise; management said it is tracking better than plan, with a visible path over the next one to two years.
Opex-to-AUM expected to move on plan, with 300-400 branches invested in per year and gold branches breaking even in about 13 months.
Management targets a sustainable ROA with a 'peak' expected in about 2.5-3 years; a commitment on ROA by June 2028 was referenced.
A 25 bps lending rate increase was already passed through about a week before the call; pass-through of further hikes is expected to depend on product and market.
AUM CAGR target of 35-40% over the next couple of years was referenced by an analyst; management did not restate it.
Management aims for consumer durable customer franchise to roughly double this year.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network at 550 branches, targeting about 200 new branches in FY27.
AI portfolio at 143 projects (up from 101), of which 84 are live in production and 59 underway; 34 delivered in Q2, a record quarter.
Collections capacity expanded with product-segmented expert teams and AI-led predictive analytics.
Commercial vehicle channel partners at 1,250; education consultant network at 700; consumer durable dealers at 20,000.
demand_pricing: Portfolio yield 14.08%, up about 45 bps QoQ; disbursement yield up about 20 bps QoQ after roughly 50 bps rise last quarter.
New products contributed 28% of disbursements (26% in Q1, 24% before that).
Management cites a gap of about 200 bps between portfolio yield and disbursement yield.
Digital-led AI campaigns reported 1.5-2x higher click-through rates, with outreach to more than 15 lakh leads per month at 60%+ lower cost than agencies.
Management flagged possible fee compression from a proposed insurance commission regulation but said earnings could absorb it.

qa_highlights.question: How far has cross-sell progressed (products per customer now vs a year or two ago), and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a products-per-customer figure; said cross-sell has only just started and the metric will be more relevant in about a year, with improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How many new products are profitable, and what blended ROA is possible once they mature?
qa_highlights.answer: No product-level count given. Management said gold branches break even in about 13 months, new businesses are not yet at full ROA, and peak ROA is expected in about 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will credit cost settle, and how will product mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 2.19% a first milestone that looks structural. CRO said 12 MoB 90-plus for origination post September 2024 improved by over 53% versus the book 12 months earlier, and credit cost is tracking better than plan.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50 bps repo hike and fixed vs floating mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of borrowing rose minimally during the tightening; NCDs are about 30% of borrowings and fixed-rate; pricing power allows pass-through. A 25 bps increase was already passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Trade-off between growth and profitability; sustainable ROA and the split of ROA gains between operating leverage and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three levers (spread, opex-to-AUM, credit cost) contribute over the next two years. Quarterly opex may fluctuate because of AI investment; no specific split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality improvement from underwriting or benign credit conditions? Are AI/ML models reducing loss rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to proprietary models (30-35 models) and calibration. It cited bureau data showing consumer durable borrowers completing 9-month loans are about 40% better credit than industry.

qa_highlights.question: With most of the book under 12 months seasoned, why are write-offs still high, and what is the impact of the insurance commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said slippages were contained across stages and GNPA and write-offs are falling; core credit cost impairment is stable in absolute terms despite over 10% QoQ book growth. On insurance commissions, management said fee compression could be absorbed by lending spreads and operating leverage.

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest income incl. fees and other income

financial_highlights.change: +16 bps QoQ, +86 bps YoY (NIM alone per CFO)

risks_watch: Opex-to-average AUM at 4.15% with ongoing frontloaded spend on collections, AI and gold branches; management warned quarterly opex may fluctuate and that it will not shy away from investments.

Rate-hike cycle: management passed through a 25 bps lending rate increase about a week before the call; further pass-through depends on product and market, and cost of borrowing rose to 7.76% from 7.72%.
Insurance commission regulation could compress fee income; management said lending spreads and operating leverage should absorb it, but no quantified impact was given.

Write-offs remain elevated despite low book seasoning (an analyst cited 60-65% of book under 12 months seasoned); management said write-offs and GNPA should fall as the book seasons, but gave no write-off figure.
Cross-sell and products-per-customer metrics were not quantified; management said the metric will be relevant in about a year, so progress is hard to verify next quarter.
Mix shift to new products (28% of disbursements) and ROA peak expected in about 2.5-3 years; the new businesses are not yet at full ROA, and June 2028 ROA commitment was referenced.
key_quotes: This quarter, in my view, marks an inflection point in establishing a self -sustaining earnings engine through the structural improvements across four key dimensions.
we've reached a substantial, I would call it, the first level of milestones of 2.19 %, which looks more structural and stable.
you won't have our product per customer journey, like I said, is just starting.
I can assure you this is structural, it's not cyclical and a choice of products also gives us strength.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on credit cost, asset quality and ROA trajectory, repeatedly calling the 2.19% credit cost structural and the trend "strength-to-strength". More cautious on specifics: declined to give products-per-customer, product-level profitability counts, or a quantified insurance-commission impact, and deflected the write-off question to seasoning arguments.
